cause.summary: The paper's site distributed only the main component (HPRD.net: 8,776 proteins, 35,820 interactions); HPRD Release 7 itself is no longer distributed.

items.label: Sec. 2.1, 189 genes outside their disease's intervals

cause.summary: Needs the 2008 UniProt gene loci, which were not distributed; the candidate file already holds every gene in an interval of its disease, with the 189 assigned.
evidence: locus_disease_preds-HPRD-LOC: all 2,068 known pairs are candidates

items.label: Methods rerun from the paper's text against the authors' prediction files

assumptions.what: Prop starts its flow at zero, F(0) = 0.
assumptions.sensitivity: Starting at the prior Y changes the scores by a median 8e-5 (relative, up to 7%) and matches none of 17,406 tested pairs; F(0) = 0 matches all to 5e-12.

assumptions.what: OPHID's RW and Prop scores use a self-interaction on every protein (HPRD's use only HPRD's own 1,839).
assumptions.sensitivity: Without them OPHID RW scores differ by a median 14% (131 of 208,509 equal); with them all 208,509 are equal.

assumptions.what: MCL is the micans.org program, release 14-137, inflation 2.0 (the supplement's value); the authors' release is not stated.
assumptions.sensitivity: Its clusters give all 386,070 MCL scores of both networks exactly.

check.detail: Neighborhood, Oti, RW, Prop (diseasenet) and MCL 14-137 rerun on HPRD and OPHID: 1,935,350 of 1,935,350 candidate-pair scores equal the authors' prediction files (relative difference below 1e-9; the files print 12 digits); without linkage intervals, 49,538 of 49,538 scores in the thresholded HPRD-NOLOC files.

items.label: Fig. 2a, consensus Random Forest (5 points)

assumptions.what: Weka 3.6.6 RandomForest with its defaults (10 trees, 4 features per split, seed 1); 13 features (Oti1-3 as 0/1, GS-All as the largest GS score); 10-fold stratified cross-validation, our split (seed 1); predicted when the yes probability >= theta.

items.label: Supp. Table 1, scores of the literature-backed associations

cause.summary: Three RW scores differ in the last printed digit: the table truncates where we round (9.87e-5 printed 9.8e-5; 2.39e-4 as 2.3e-4; 6.17e-4 as 6.1e-4), but ATM's 2.68e-3 is printed rounded (2.7e-3). Four other entries are decimal slips (exceptions).

hypotheses.hypothesis: The table truncates instead of rounding.
hypotheses.test: Explains PRMT2, PSMA5 and MYC; ATM is rounded.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The authors' RW scores without intervals differ from ours.
hypotheses.test: Our rerun equals all 7,201 RW scores of the authors' HPRD-NOLOC file.

exceptions.evidence: Ours 0.0123: the table's 0.12 is ten times larger. ALOX5's Prop for the same disease (0.18) equals ours (0.182), so the scale is the same.
Ours 0.0183, printed 0.18 (a decimal slip, as for PRMT2).
Ours 0.0173, printed 0.17 (a decimal slip, as for PRMT2).
Ours 0.077 (1 of 13 other cluster members), printed 0.8; MCL scores are fractions k/(size - 1) and PSMA5's cluster has 14 members.

items.label: Graph summarization (GS1-3, GS-All) rerun

cause.summary: The graph summarization code was never released with the paper; Navlakha's page linked it to an Alcatel-Lucent page that no archive captured. GS scores are used from the authors' prediction files.

items.label: VI-Cut (VI-CutS, VI-CutL) rerun

cause.summary: The authors' VI-Cut code survives (vicut.zip, Wayback 2012), but its input, the tree of the modified graph-summarization merge process, is lost with the GS code. VI-Cut scores are used from the authors' prediction files.
